role.altitude: The two analysts stop assembling Excel packs and take ownership of the cost drivers, the cost-centre hierarchy and the forecast rules. They keep the analysis, the recommendations and the conversations with managers, the board and the bank. Data pulls, variance tables and first drafts become scheduled jobs that the analysts review.
reach: controller: month-close checks and the budget-to-actual bridge use the same AFAS extract and mapping table
people-analyst: headcount and flex-worker cost drivers come from the same AFAS and agency data
finance-director: funds decisions and board and bank packs are built on the analysts' drafts
bookkeeper: agency invoices and accruals feed the flex-cost lines in every cost model
skills_to_grow: Defining cost drivers (FTE, CAO shift allowances, flex hours, volumes) as data, not as spreadsheet formulas
SQL and Power BI semantic models on the AFAS extract
Reviewing model-drafted commentary against the source figures
Writing funds recommendations that set out options and their trade-offs
Change control for budget transfers and the cost-centre hierarchy
role.ambitious_version: A monthly rolling forecast for each of the three sites. It runs on defined volume, headcount and flex-rate drivers, and the budget pack, the funds-request check and the contingency register all come from one governed AFAS extract. The analysts spend their time on driver quality, peak-season scenarios and talks with site managers.

tasks.short: Work out what a new initiative will cost, such as an extra shift, a new client or peak-season flex staffing.

steps.what: Pull GL, agency hours and headcount data for the affected cost centres
Agree scope, volumes and start date with the requesting manager
Build the cost model from drivers: FTE, CAO rates, shift allowances, flex hours
Sanity-check the result against history and similar past initiatives
Write the resource summary for the requester and the controller

loop.input: checked cost model figures and assumption list
loop.output: one-page resource summary in plain Dutch or English
loop.check: Every number in the text is matched by code to a cell in the model; any mismatch blocks the draft
loop.stop: Two redrafts at most, then fall back to a fixed template with the table only
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot explain which assumptions drive the cost; a short model-written paragraph can, and the number check keeps it honest

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on a governed data store pulls AFAS GetConnector data (GL, cost centres, headcount) and the agency hours and invoices into one cost base. An Excel or Power BI template then applies defined drivers (CAO rates, shift allowances, agency rates) to the scope the analyst enters. A bounded model step drafts the summary text, and code checks every figure in it against the model.
tasks.previous_blocker: The data sat in three places (AFAS, three agency portals, personal Excel). Driver logic lived in each analyst's spreadsheet, so nothing could be reused or scheduled.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes small extract jobs and driver templates cheap to build and maintain. Models can draft explanatory text that code checks against the numbers.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing the drivers and keeping the CAO and agency rate tables current. Agency portals may only offer file exports, not APIs. The volume assumptions come from managers and stay uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a manager's volume and timing assumptions are realistic, and knowing which past initiative is a fair comparison.

ambition.what: Cost every client tender and shift change before it is agreed, not only the large ones

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends their time on scoping talks and checking assumptions instead of pulling data. They own the driver and rate tables that every cost model uses.

reach.learn: How the AFAS headcount and agency hours are defined, so cost drivers and HR figures agree
How agency rates, surcharges and invoice timing show up in the GL

evidence.claim: Finance executives report AI more useful than expected for budgeting (+42 net) and model building (+27 net)
Agents gather data, flag records that do not tie and do variance arithmetic; people decide which source wins
AI speed does not fix undefined drivers or unclean data, and can hide existing errors
AFAS Profit exposes GL and HR data through GetConnectors

assumptions: Noordhaven has or can get a governed data store (for example Azure SQL or Fabric) next to the nightly Power BI extract
The CAO wage and allowance tables can be kept as a maintained table
Initiative costs are at cost-centre level and do not need named individuals
unknowns: Whether the three agency portals offer APIs or only CSV and PDF exports
How many initiative costings the analysts do each month and of what size
Whether a shared driver model would be accepted by site managers
research_questions: Can 80% of past initiative costings be rebuilt from a fixed driver set (FTE, CAO rate, shift allowance, flex hours, volume)?
Do the agency portals provide hours and rates per cost centre in a machine-readable export?
How far did past initiative cost estimates differ from actuals, and which assumptions caused the gap?

tasks.short: Review site and department funds requests against budget and recommend approval or rejection to the finance director.

steps.what: Receive the funds request by mail and log it
Check the request against remaining budget and open commitments
Analyse the business case, payback and alternatives
Draft the recommendation memo with options

loop.input: request form fields, headroom check and the analyst's analysis notes
loop.output: memo draft with the request, budget position, options and a proposed recommendation marked as draft
loop.check: Code matches all amounts to the headroom check and the request; the analyst must edit or confirm the recommendation line
loop.stop: One draft plus one redraft, then a fixed template with only the facts filled in
loop.why_not_simpler: The business case arrives as free text, and the memo has to weigh it in prose; a template covers the figures but not the reasoning

steps.what: Discuss with the finance director, record the decision and inform the requester

tasks.design: Replace the mailbox and Excel log with a Microsoft Form and SharePoint list, routed by Power Automate. A scheduled check against the AFAS extract shows remaining budget and commitments for the cost centre in Power BI. A bounded model step drafts the memo from the analyst's notes, and the finance director's decision is recorded in the list and sent back to the requester automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came in by mail in any format, and budget headroom needed a manual AFAS and Excel lookup each time. Memo writing was not worth templating for the volume.
tasks.enabler_now: Microsoft 365 already has Forms, Lists and Power Automate. AI coding makes the headroom check quick to build. A model can draft a memo from structured fields and notes, with a code check on the figures.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether the business case is sound and how the request fits company priorities. Open commitments may not all be in AFAS when the check runs.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing a site manager's case against the company's priorities and cash position. Telling a manager no and keeping the relationship.

ambition.what: Give a decision within one week on every funds request above a set threshold, with a monthly overview of approved spend per site

tasks.altitude: The analyst no longer chases forms or looks up budgets. Their week is spent on the business cases and on proposing approval thresholds to the finance director.

reach.learn: Which criteria the director actually weighs, so the memo puts them first
Which commitments are missing from AFAS at the time of the check

evidence.claim: A model step can draft a recommendation memo while a person decides
The least successful AI finance tasks are those that demand human judgement
People decide capital allocation; agents gather data and draft commentary
In finance a good guess is not good enough

assumptions: Funds requests are about cost centres and assets, not named employees
Power Automate and SharePoint Lists are licensed in the M365 tenant
Purchase orders and commitments are recorded in AFAS
unknowns: How many funds requests arrive each month and the approval thresholds that apply
Whether managers would accept a standard request form
Who approves at which amount under the current mandate rules
research_questions: What share of past funds requests could have been decided on budget headroom alone?
Are open commitments in AFAS complete enough for a reliable headroom check?
Does the finance director find model-drafted memos with options faster to decide on than today's mails?

tasks.short: Produce the monthly budget-versus-actual pack per site and cost centre, plus ad hoc reports.

steps.what: Refresh actuals and budget data and fix cost-centre mapping breaks
Build variance tables per site and cost centre
Chase cost-centre owners for variance explanations
Write variance commentary for the pack

loop.input: variance table above the threshold and the owners' explanations
loop.output: commentary per site in a fixed structure: line, amount, cause, action
loop.check: Code checks every amount and percentage against the variance table; lines without an owner explanation are marked 'no explanation received'
loop.stop: One redraft on a failed check, then the line shows the figure only
loop.why_not_simpler: Owners write explanations as free text in mixed Dutch and English; turning them into consistent commentary needs reading, not rules

steps.what: Review the pack with the controller and send it out

tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel pack with a scheduled job that loads the AFAS extract and budget into a governed store and fills a Power BI paginated report per site. Power Automate sends each cost-centre owner their lines above a threshold with a short form to explain them. A bounded model step drafts the commentary from those answers, and the analyst and controller review the pack before it goes out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost-centre mapping changed by hand in Excel each month, and explanations came back by mail in any form. The pack needed someone to stitch it together.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI is already in use and AI coding makes the extract, mapping checks and report templates fast to build. Models can turn free-text explanations into consistent commentary, with numbers checked by code.
tasks.still_hard: Getting owners to explain on time, and keeping the mapping table right when cost centres change. Copilot in Power BI needs a prepared model and is not officially supported in Dutch. Faster packs may invite more report requests.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which variances matter for the business and telling a site manager or the board what it means.

ambition.what: A mid-month flash report per site for site managers, built from the same pipeline

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops building tables and chasing mails. They review commentary, decide the variance thresholds and spend time with site managers on the large variances.

reach.learn: Which close adjustments land after the pack is built, so the pack waits for them or flags them
Which staffing decisions drive the largest cost variances

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI summarises reports but needs a prepared semantic model, and non-English use is not officially supported
Agents draft commentary and do variance arithmetic in current FP&A products
The most AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor

assumptions: The budget is held in a file or AFAS budget table that can be loaded
Packs are sent internally and to the board; bank reporting uses the same figures
Variance thresholds can be set per site and per line
unknowns: How many regular and special reports are made each month
Whether the bank requires a fixed report format
Which Power BI licence or capacity Noordhaven has
research_questions: How many hours does the current pack take each month, and which part is mapping repair?
Do cost-centre owners answer a short form faster than a mail thread?
Do the controller and finance director accept model-drafted commentary after review, or rewrite most of it?

tasks.short: Reconcile cost-centre budgets to site and company totals and track the contingency reserve.

steps.what: Export cost-centre budgets and actuals from AFAS
Map cost centres to the site and company hierarchy
Reconcile sub-budgets to site and total budgets and list breaks
Track contingency reserve draws and reallocations
Post approved budget transfers in AFAS

tasks.design: Hold the cost-centre hierarchy as a maintained dimension in AFAS or a small governed mapping table instead of an Excel tab. A scheduled Python job reconciles every sub-budget to its site and company total after each AFAS refresh, lists breaks, and keeps a contingency register in a SharePoint list or small app. Approved transfers are posted to AFAS through its update connector after the controller signs off.
tasks.previous_blocker: The hierarchy and the contingency reserve lived in Excel tabs that only the analysts understood. Transfers were typed into AFAS by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes reconciliation scripts and a small register app cheap. AFAS connectors allow reading and posting budget lines without screen work.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the hierarchy right when cost centres are added or merged. Deciding who may draw on the contingency reserve. AFAS write access needs tight control and an audit trail.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether an overrun should come from contingency or be absorbed by the site, and explaining that choice to the controller.

ambition.what: Show contingency use and remaining reserve per site every week instead of at quarter end

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops rebuilding the reconciliation each month. They own the hierarchy, review breaks and propose reallocations for the controller to approve.

reach.task: Approving budget transfers and the close
reach.learn: Which transfers need an audit trail and which mandate limits apply
How new or merged cost centres are set up, so the hierarchy changes at the same time

evidence.claim: Agents flag records that do not tie; people decide which source wins
Clean data, certified reports and defined drivers are preconditions; speed makes existing errors harder to catch
Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%)
AFAS Profit supports reading and updating data through GetConnectors and UpdateConnectors

assumptions: Noordhaven keeps a contingency or emergency reserve in the budget
Budgets are held per cost centre in AFAS
The controller approves all budget transfers
unknowns: Whether the hierarchy can be held in AFAS itself or needs a separate table
How often cost centres change during the year
Who may approve contingency draws, and up to what amount
research_questions: How many reconciliation breaks per month come from hierarchy changes versus real budget errors?
Can AFAS budget transfers be posted by connector with an audit trail the auditor accepts?
Would a weekly contingency view change any decision by the controller or site managers?
